newsitem.title: UK: World wheat prices extend a slide.
newsitem.headline: World wheat prices extend a slide.

text.p: World wheat prices are sliding in a retreat from historic highs that reflects bumper harvests in Europe, Australia and China.

Values in the European Union were under new pressure this week. A Reuters survey of EU grains prices on Wednesday showed fresh declines in tandem with weaker US futures on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
The declines bring relief to cash-pinched Third World buyers. Bumper crops have followed droughts in 1994 which had depressed world food stocks to the lowest in 20 years.
Chicago futures below $3.75 per bushel now contrast with several months ago when they were above $5.00 and a spike in March to a record $7.50.

Benchmark French wheat delivered to Rouen for November traded this week at $162 per tonne, compared with $169 a month ago and traders are looking for fresh export subsidies from the EU in Brussels this week.

But so far the EU has not given subsidies that quite cover a a French sale of 150,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Egypt that values it down at $146.50-$147 for fear of provoking the United States into a subsidy war. A cautionary note on food costs was sounded this week by Brokerage GNI Ltd, however, when its latest Commodity Perspective said grain stocks were still low and "the wheat market is very oversold".
And "bullish" input from a new crop estimate on Wednesday helped boost CBOT maize (corn) and soybeans futures.
Traders said Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies pegged 1996 US maize production at 9.147 billion bushels and soybeans at 2.367 billion.
The market was expecting a 9.3 billion on maize and 2.4 billion for soybeans, traders said.

Excitement in equities and bonds over the US elections and apparent success of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery has yet to spill over to commodity markets although a firm dollar pressured gold.
It closed in London at $378.15 after $379.45 an ounce on Tuesday. The world benchmark Brent Blend of crude oil was trading around $22.50 per barrel, little changed from late Tuesday afternoon.
Elsewhere in commodity markets, aluminium, copper, coffee and cocoa were just firmer from Tuesday. Sugar extended a technical decline.
